name: Alignment, Ride Height & Corner-Weight Setup
description: Setup targets and procedures performed at phase 11: ride height, corner weights, final torque of all rubber-bushed TTY pivots at ride height, and four-wheel alignment. Factory values are approximate (GM alignment specs by RPO are in GM SI and the Chevrolet Camaro Track Preparation Guide); race values are typical starting points for a Gen 6 road-race car.

components.name: Front alignment targets (camber, caster, toe)
components.description: Front camber is set with camber plates (or by link length with adjustable LCAs); caster is set with camber/caster plates or adjustable radius rods (factory caster is not adjustable); toe with the tie rods. Equalize caster within approx 0.2 deg side-to-side for straight-line stability under braking.

factory.name: GM factory alignment (approximate)
factory.notes: Camber approx -0.5 to -1.0 deg (street); ZL1 1LE track top-mount position adds negative camber; caster approx 6.5-7.7 deg (fixed); total toe approx 0 to +0.1 deg in. Values are estimates - confirm against GM SI / Track Preparation Guide for your RPO.

raceOptions.name: Typical road-race targets
raceOptions.notes: Camber -2.7 to -3.5 deg (200TW street tires toward -2.7/-3.2; slicks toward -3.5 or more); caster 7.5-9.0 deg (equal L/R); total toe 0 to 1/16 in out (0 to -0.1 deg). Owner-reported 2020 ZL1 1LE track alignment with BMR/SPL parts: -3.2 deg front camber, 7.6-7.7 deg caster.

installNotes: Set ride height and corner weights first.
Driver weight (or ballast) in seat, fuel at race level, tire pressures at target.
Final-torque all front TTY pivot bolts at ride height before aligning.
inspection: Re-check after any curb strike or off.

components.name: Rear alignment targets (camber, toe)
components.description: Rear camber is set by the LCA inner eccentric (or adjustable upper/lower links) and toe by the toe-link inner eccentric (or adjustable toe links). OE eccentrics offer approx 1 deg of range; lock them out or use adjustable links for racing.

factory.name: GM factory rear alignment (approximate)
factory.notes: Camber approx -0.7 to -1.2 deg; total toe approx +0.1 to +0.2 deg in. Estimates - confirm in GM SI.

raceOptions.name: Typical road-race targets
raceOptions.notes: Camber -1.5 to -2.2 deg (owner-reported ZL1 1LE track alignments -1.8 to -2.0 deg); total toe 1/16-1/8 in in (approx 0.1-0.25 deg). Never run rear toe-out.

installNotes: Final-torque LCA inner cam bolt (115 N·m + 90-105 deg) and toe cam bolt (70 N·m + 90-105 deg) after setting, with new bolts.

components.name: Ride height, rake and corner weights
components.description: Set on level scale pads with driver (or ballast) and race fuel load. Adjust threaded perches (coilovers / ZL1 1LE front: approx 1.5 mm per turn) to reach target ride heights and approx 50% cross weight (LF+RR). Lowering a strut car too far drops the front roll center below ground and worsens bump steer - correct with roll-center spacers/links and bump-steer tie rod ends rather than just going lower.

factory.name: Factory trim height
factory.notes: GM SG3 kit lowers approx 20 mm; ZL1 1LE front perch +/-10 mm.

raceOptions.name: Typical race starting point
raceOptions.notes: Lower approx 25-40 mm from stock, slight positive rake (rear higher) for splitter/diffuser cars; check splitter height and class minimums; 50% cross weight.

specs.Rear natural frequency (typical): approx 10-15% above or near front depending on philosophy

installNotes: Disconnect sway bar end links while corner weighting, then reconnect with zero preload.
Bounce/roll the car between measurements to settle bushings.

components.name: Final torque of rubber-bushed TTY pivots at ride height
components.description: Checklist step: every rubber-bushed pivot (front LCA and radius rod inner bolts; rear LCA, UCA, trailing arm and toe-link bolts) must be final-torqued with the suspension at normal ride height, using new torque-to-yield bolts. Torquing at full droop pre-twists the bushings, raising ride height and causing premature bushing failure. Paint-mark every bolt after torque.

raceOptions.name: Spherical-bearing links
raceOptions.notes: Spherical bearings do not need ride-height torquing but still follow fastener specs.

installNotes: Use drive-on ramps/pit pads or jack each knuckle to measured ride height.
Use an angle gauge for the angle step.
